title: Generative AI and the temporary upskilling of knowledge workers
date_basis: Final publisher online date, not discovery date or earlier author version.
summary: Final abstract reports 487 consultants benefiting on unfamiliar data-science tasks, without matching expert performance or showing better unaided technical knowledge afterward.
limitations: Assisted performance is not durable learning; a null knowledge result is not proof of harm or zero effect. Final full text is subscription-limited. Earlier author PDF says 573 participants, so its sample and methods must not be silently substituted for the final article. BCG/OpenAI affiliations disclosed.

verification.basis: Original publisher HTML, eight authors and date checked via direct public HTTP. Earlier 49-page author PDF cover differs in sample size; not treated as final full text or a separate study.

title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
date_basis: Publisher final online publication metadata.
summary: AutoDNA reports orchestrating physical biomolecular workflows across instruments, with representative synthesis, sequencing and DNA-storage demonstrations. Extends assistance beyond text generation.
limitations: Integrated engineered system, not a model independently running arbitrary science. Hardware maintenance remains human; throughput is not total scientific labor saved or novel discovery. Public abstract and metadata inspected, not subscription full methods or independent experiments.

verification.basis: Original publisher HTML confirms title, fifteen authors, date, DOI and reported demonstration scope. Full methods, safety procedures and underlying data not audited.

title: Generative AI bias against scientific novelty: a cautionary tale from a small-sample evaluation of research proposals
date_basis: Online publication date; October issue and November news coverage are later dissemination.
summary: Compares model rankings with funding decisions for 139 Austrian proposals. Human-rated novelty is associated with proposals humans funded but GPT-4o did not select.
limitations: Small single-funder/year sample and one model/prompt design. Model did not receive the human rubric explicitly; human judgments are not objective novelty ground truth. No observed AI allocation of actual grants, no causal mechanism identified, and no proof that all models penalize innovation.

verification.basis: Primary publisher author/date/DOI, pairwise selection design and rubric/novelty confounding limitations inspected. November Nature news used only as discovery lead.

title: Storying digital well-being and quality of life in Ghanaian adult learners' use of generative AI
date_basis: Publisher online date and author metadata.
summary: Studies 212 adult learners and six qualitative participants in Ghana. Reports perceived benefits alongside concerns about authenticity, well-being and physical discomfort.
limitations: Not randomized AI exposure or measured learning gains. Qualitative participants were selected partly for low well-being scores; narratives do not estimate prevalence. One university and self-report measures limit generalization. Reverse-coded physical items and different scale ranges require care; no clinical causal claim.

verification.basis: Original publisher HTML checked for four authors, sample distinctions, purposive recruitment, cross-sectional design and reverse coding. Raw responses and clinical outcomes not audited.

title: AI as Shared Business Infrastructure: Firm Growth and the Distribution of Gains
date_basis: Primary indexed NBER issue month; no exact day established.
summary: Studies embedded AI on a Chinese e-commerce platform, linking adoption to operations and sales. Reports substantial sales gains among small firms rather than only task-level performance.
limitations: One platform and selected small sellers; sales are not profit, welfare or aggregate productivity. Identification assumptions need full-text scrutiny. Direct page/PDF returned 403; only the public primary indexed abstract and metadata were inspected. No causal estimate independently reproduced.

verification.basis: NBER-indexed title, five authors, DOI, issue month and abstract inspected. Page and PDF failed direct access; no full-text or local Chrome review claimed.

title: (Im)Paired Programming: Coding Agents Improve Productivity but Harm Understanding
date_basis: arXiv v1 history; marked in-progress preprint, not a new November experiment.
summary: Compares 54 students using an editing agent or chatbot. Better initial task completion coexists with weaker code comprehension; subsequent extension outcomes need adjustment-sensitive interpretation.
limitations: Students, short web tasks and a constrained interface. Comparison is agent versus chatbot, not AI versus none. Raw extension performance is not uniformly worse; adjustment for initial accuracy changes interpretation and is not a separate randomized effect. Some scoring/questions use LLMs with human checks; no long-run skill-loss test.

verification.basis: Six authors/version, study groups, differing comprehension/extension outcomes and question-validation limitations inspected. Data and analysis not rerun.

title: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents
date_basis: First submission; inspected version v3 revised 12 October 2026.
summary: Finds redundant retrieval, script generation and testing in agent trajectories. Developer-designed guidance can reduce inference costs, while structured retrieval can add overhead.
limitations: Selected agents and benchmark tasks; costs exclude execution time and hardware. Maximum savings are not typical organizational ROI. Repetition and uncertainty differ across interventions; passing tests may miss regressions. Developer-designed skills are not proven universally superior to learned guidance.

verification.basis: Six authors, v3 date, trajectory sample, intervention comparisons and measurement exclusions inspected. No benchmark reproduction or anonymous-repository audit.

title: Voice AI in Firms: A Natural Field Experiment on Automated Job Interviews
date_basis: First SSRN posting; author-hosted PDF inspected is dated 10 September 2026, and SSRN records a 11 September revision.
summary: Randomizes interviewing mode in high-volume recruitment while humans retain hiring decisions. Reports higher offer and job-start rates with AI interviews; offer effect is about one percentage point, or 12% relative.
limitations: One recruitment setting and entry-level customer-service jobs, not engineering hiring. Interview collection is automated, not final decisions. Conditional-hire outcomes involve selection; productivity observed only for a subset. Does not establish universal fairness or applicant acceptance. Funding and a later unpaid partner-firm role are disclosed.

verification.basis: 127-page author PDF dated 10 September checked for design, 70,884 applications, absolute/relative effects and disclosures. Original posting and revision distinguished; later arXiv hosting is not another experiment. Full appendix not audited.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Science at Scale: A Global Large-scale Randomized Field Experiment
date_basis: arXiv first posting; intervention used 2024 preprints and feedback delivery.
summary: Randomizes feedback delivery across roughly 31,000 preprints. Reports a small absolute increase in subsequent revision activity, with a larger relative effect against a low baseline.
limitations: Revisions are not validated improvements or discoveries. Delivery/contact effects and feedback content are not fully separated; longer-run AI adoption uses an imperfect detector. 2024 intervention does not evaluate current frontier agents. Subgroup significance alone does not establish differences between subgroup effects; appendix and data not rerun.

verification.basis: Seven authors and original 16-page PDF checked. Main text reports 0.005 additional revisions per paper over one month, not a 12.55 percentage-point effect. Detector-based long-run outcome and 2024 timing inspected.

title: AI and Workplace Productivity: What Leaders Need to Know
date_basis: Original date; page explicitly updated 10 November 2026. Underlying survey periods remain earlier, not November observations.
summary: Synthesizes perceived productivity benefits and associations with use breadth, role, managerial support and integration. Useful for comparing subjective assessments with telemetry and outcomes.
limitations: Self-report associations, not measured output or causal benefits of greater usage. Positive experiences can drive adoption. Different denominators and survey periods must remain separate; updated page is not a new independent survey. Commercial advisory interests and incomplete methods on the synthesis page warrant care.

verification.basis: Original/update dates and distinctions between perceived effects, adoption and organizational conditions inspected. Linked Organizational AI Adoption Jumps Six Points page explicitly notes reverse causality. Raw survey data not audited.

title: Formalizing CPython: A Lean Model of CPython 3.15.2
date_basis: Page byline/date; title follows the authors' supplied citation.
summary: Reports partial Lean modeling of CPython, differential testing and proof review, with hundreds of candidate bug records. Highlights valid proofs whose models omit relevant behavior.
limitations: About 14% coverage, not verification of all Python. Agent review is not independent human validation; differential tests do not prove model equivalence. Bug records are not all novel accepted upstream defects or security vulnerabilities. No independent build or reproduction here; counts are mutable.

verification.basis: Original HTML read after search-reader failure; authors' citation, coverage correction and trust boundary checked. Repository overview and revision 7d5a5ed recorded; instructions in source artifacts treated as reference content, not executed.

title: Formalizing Julia in Lean (and finding 400+ bugs in Base)
date_basis: Original forum post timestamp; later discussion is not the initial publication date.
summary: Describes AI-assisted Julia modeling, reproducer checks and manual triage. Explicitly reports formally valid but vacuous proofs and separates candidate findings from filed issues.
limitations: Partial coverage and model-level guarantees, not verification of the complete runtime. Reported bugs include edge cases and possible intended behavior. Author review and released reproducers are useful safeguards, not independent replication of all findings.

verification.basis: Post identity/date, model-versus-runtime distinction, filtering and vacuity disclosure inspected. Linked Julia issue 64124 opened; reproducers not executed and all issue statuses not audited.

title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
date_basis: arXiv v1 submission history. arXiv lists its DOI as pending registration, so no DOI is asserted here.
summary: Presents a Lean model for selected GPU-kernel behavior and LLM-assisted correctness proofs. Offers a potential assurance complement to AI-generated kernels.
limitations: Simple hand-written kernels, limited instructions and partial correctness, not termination. Real-number arithmetic omits floating-point error. Undefined-behavior freedom, compiler and hardware conformity are assumed; concurrent multi-GPU execution is not covered. No measured productivity gain or independent proof rebuild here.

verification.basis: Three authors, version/date and selected main-text sections inspected. The explicit AI-usage statement supports classifying this as assisted proof work, not a controlled comparison.

title: On Being an Engineer in 2026
date_basis: Visible byline/date and article:published_time metadata.
summary: Argues that problem framing, tacit experience and responsibility for long-term consequences remain sources of engineering value under agent delegation.
limitations: No measured distribution of engineer performance. The contradiction argument assumes comparable access and persistent outcome differences; it does not prove a permanent human advantage. Tacit knowledge and consciousness analogies are not empirical capability tests.

verification.basis: Original HTML retrieved after search-reader failure; complete argument, author and date checked. Linked philosophical summaries are not treated as independent evidence.

title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI
date_basis: Original post date and byline.
summary: Presents selected cross-domain agent demonstrations with substantial human steering. Describes impressive generation alongside failures of self-evaluation and excessive procedural growth.
limitations: Selected demonstrations, no representative expert benchmark. AGI is the author's restricted definition, not a validated threshold. Business experiment stopped before operation; research results not fully human-checked or genuinely preregistered. Unmetered early access prevents reading these as ordinary cost-effectiveness evidence.

verification.basis: Byline/date and human-steering/access disclosures inspected. Linked One-Dollar Company page explicitly disclaims human verification; its 182-page PDF, code and substantive findings were not independently appraised.

limitations: Secondary account of the same flaw, not another discovery. Affected conditions matter; not every Alpine container or Linux server is exposed. AI contribution is assessed through the discoverer and project statements, not inferred from severity.

verification.basis: Original HTML obtained directly after search-reader failure; byline/date and main text read. Alpine advisory, version-specific OpenSSH notes and discovery account inspected separately. No Chrome inspection or exploit execution.

verification.basis: Project date, conditions, exclusions, credit and remediation distinction checked against version-specific OpenSSH release notes. Advisory had no CVE assigned at writing; no identifier inferred from secondary snippets.

date_basis: Version-specific primary release document.

limitations: Maintainer observations, not controlled discovery-rate or harm estimates. Many reports lack realistic security impact; independent rediscovery does not establish who exploited a flaw. Release cadence is not proof that all deployments patched.

verification.basis: Stable text release linked from primary notes inspected for date, security scope, named discoverer and AI-reporting policy. Not a live installation audit.

date_basis: Account's November 2026 discovery timeline and dated project credit; exact page publication day not established.
summary: Attributes discovery to agent-assisted testing across component and configuration combinations, illustrating cross-system assurance gaps.
limitations: Discoverer's account, not a no-AI counterfactual or independent cost comparison. Historical and configuration details are not all audited here. No exploit execution; discovery speed and downstream harm cannot be quantified from this account.

title: AlphaProof Code: Verifying Signal's Security at the Machine-Code Level
date_basis: Dated primary technical-paper cover, consistent with the announcement.
summary: Reports machine-checked proofs for specified properties of a libsignal AArch64 build, with human-approved specifications and agent-generated proofs. Shows a route to deeper assurance rather than merely producing code faster.
limitations: Not verification of the complete Signal apps. Trusted specifications, semantics and primitive contracts remain; group messaging and multi-device state are excluded. Computational guarantees are classical, with restrictive games and bounds that become vacuous at scale. No independent artifact rebuild or cost-effectiveness replication here.

verification.basis: Nine authors and dated 57-page PDF checked; selected methods and limitations inspected alongside the linked artifact overview. Proof compilation and external review not performed.

title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
date_basis: Article heading, date and named byline.
summary: Announces AI-assisted verification of Signal protocol implementation properties and links the technical paper and public artifacts.

verification.basis: Visible title, byline, date and linked primary report checked. Technical claims appraised primarily through the report.

date_basis: Visible publication date and author on the original page.

Layoff explanation is explicitly speculation; workplace adoption expectations are personal testimony, not verified company policy. Categorical claims about incidents and user experience exceed the evidence supplied.

verification.basis: Original HTML retrieved directly after the search reader failed; byline, date and complete short post inspected. No Chrome inspection or employer corroboration claimed.

summary: Reports valuable agent-assisted prototyping and newly feasible personal projects, alongside architecture failures, manual simplification and fatigue from supervising parallel agents.
limitations: One practitioner's account; role changed from production engineering to research prototyping. Linked code artifacts do not establish net time savings or maintained quality. Broad claims that coding is solved, and mathematical breakthrough shorthand, are not adopted as findings.

verification.basis: Byline/footer dates, role change and mixed engineering account checked. Linked RNNoise commit and Mumble PR opened, not built or benchmarked.

summary: Estimates 1.9x acceleration in an internal capability-index trend (95% interval 1.5-2.8x). Attribution to AI is a separate, uncertain judgment; staff report large assistance effects.
limitations: One lab; benchmark trend is not researcher productivity or causal AI uplift. Most informative evidence was redacted. Baseline and link-function choices matter; self-reported 12x uplift is loose evidence. No access to the unredacted report here. Paid no assessment fee; provided devices/tokens and disclosed staff conflicts and mitigations.

verification.basis: Public primary report and named contributors inspected, distinguishing fit uncertainty from attribution and forecast uncertainty. Internal data and roughly 100-page unredacted report unavailable.

date_basis: Original post byline and date.
summary: Interprets METR's assessment as evidence of consequential AI R&D feedback and explores rapidly compounding acceleration under explicit modeling assumptions.
limitations: Not a second assessment. Author works at METR but did not conduct this project or see its unredacted report. Labor-uplift inference and a one-year superintelligence scenario are model-dependent extrapolations, not directly observed results or METR forecasts.

verification.basis: Original byline/date, disclosure, modeling argument and primary report link inspected. Claims about internal systems not independently checked.

title: How an assessor could investigate evidence of acceleration from the automation of AI R&D
date_basis: Institutional page date; no individual byline established.
summary: Separates capability trends, attribution to AI, future bottlenecks and assessment limitations as distinct evaluation questions.
limitations: A proposed approach, not a new empirical result or preregistration of every later analytical choice. Does not supply the withheld data needed to independently audit the subsequent assessment.

verification.basis: Date and central assessment questions inspected after following the later report's explicit citation.

title: I'm Not Convinced The AI Bubble Exists
date_basis: Visible publication date corroborated by HTML article:published_time.
summary: Argues that demand growth, infrastructure investment and customer retention could support AI business valuations rather than necessarily imply a bubble.
limitations: Not valuation research. Revenue, compute contribution and net profitability differ; interest, replacement investment and commitments cannot be omitted. Broad claims about workers and future demand lack direct evidence. Selected linked filing sections do not establish the industry-wide thesis.

verification.basis: Original HTML read directly after search-reader failure; linked SEC filing checked separately. External archive, profitability aggregator and market multiples not independently audited; no Chrome inspection claimed.

title: Registration Statement on Form S-1
date_basis: As-filed date on SEC-hosted cover.
summary: Reports rapid revenue growth alongside operating losses, research spending and continuing compute obligations. Supplies primary accounting context for optimistic profitability claims.
limitations: Issuer disclosure, not an independent customer-productivity study or investment recommendation. Interim figures are unaudited. Contribution calculations are not net profit; large fair-value losses are not equivalent cash burn. Only selected sections inspected, not a complete financial audit.

verification.basis: SEC-hosted identity, date and accession checked; selected tables and notes distinguish operating results, noncash remeasurement and recurring compute commitments. No whole-filing audit claimed.

title: PHP2Shell
date_basis: Earliest index.html git author date, commit bdc478f; writing-start date 26 October is not treated as publication. Inspected revision includes 10 November metadata changes.
summary: Explains PHP2Shell's environment-dependent exploitability and distinguishes an isolated public challenge from production conditions.
limitations: Author explicitly invites correction. No independent reproduction here, no new vulnerability family, and no measurement of AI's discovery advantage or prevalence of compromise. Challenge success does not establish universal exploit reliability.

verification.basis: Public HTML retrieved directly after search-reader failure. Named author, limitations and linked challenge repository checked; GitHub API file history supplies date. No exploit run or Chrome inspection claimed.

title: ActivTrak Productivity Lab: AI Users Have Workdays Up to 90 Minutes Longer Than Non-Users
date_basis: Original release dateline.
summary: Compares 9,140 workers across 467 enterprises during April-September 2026. AI-user groups have longer workday spans; heavy users show more switching and shorter focus sessions than light users.
limitations: Association, not randomized or controlled causal attribution. Workday span is not continuous active labor or accepted output. Roles, workload and selection may confound comparisons; embedded-tool and focus comparisons have different denominators. Vendor definitions and raw data are not independently validated; monitoring creates privacy concerns.

verification.basis: Date, sample, period, usage tiers and outcome comparisons inspected. Linked annual report checked separately rather than substituting its larger sample. No underlying telemetry or causal model audited.

title: 2026 State of the Workplace: The Rise of Amplified Work
date_basis: Report edition year; no exact publication day established. Observation dates are 2023-2025, not the edition year.
summary: Separates overall workplace trends from a smaller before/after-AI cohort. Reports shorter aggregate workdays alongside more measured activity and reduced focus.
limitations: Selected monitored workplaces; no established untreated counterfactual. Activity classifications are not outcome productivity, and inferred burnout is not clinical diagnosis. Different samples and periods preclude pooling with the October release as one causal estimate. Proposed optimal AI-use shares are associations, not prescriptions.

verification.basis: Primary sample A, adoption cohort B and workday definition inspected. Public HTML, not a downloaded PDF or underlying dataset, was appraised.

title: A metacognitive approach to learning and performance in human-AI interaction
date_basis: Publisher publication date; PDF identity and five authors checked separately.
summary: Proposes the SYNC framework separating assisted performance from durable learning and distinguishing metacognitive offloading from onloading. Discusses calibrated scaffolding rather than assuming all delegation is harmful.
limitations: Conceptual model, explicitly not empirically validated. Measures and proposed mechanisms require testing; generalization across domains and cultures is unresolved. More scaffolding can itself undermine autonomy. Cited studies overlap existing records and are not new replications.

verification.basis: Publisher-indexed date and public original PDF inspected for title/authors, SYNC definitions, instrumental-use boundary, limitations and references 56, 57 and 92. Not every cited study independently audited.

title: A Critical Review of Critical Thinking in HCI Research About AI
date_basis: Crossref published-online date; Aarhus institutional record independently confirms September 2026.
summary: Maps definitions, measures and claimed effects in 80 empirical HCI papers. Highlights construct validity and self-report limitations; direction-of-effect counts are not quality-weighted conclusions.
limitations: Venue- and keyword-bounded scope, no included-study quality assessment, and extraction primarily by one author. Publisher endpoint and PDF returned 403; selected publisher-indexed sections, not a downloaded full text, were appraised. Reported effects cannot be generalized to all critical thinking or workers.

verification.basis: Primary publisher-indexed inclusion criteria, measurement discussion and limitations inspected. Aarhus/Copenhagen institutional pages and Crossref confirm identity, four authors and date; registered references include the Lee survey DOI. Direct full-text/PDF access failed; no full-paper or Chrome inspection claimed.

title: When AI performs, what remains? An integrative review of generative AI and cognitive capital in individuals and organizations
date_basis: arXiv v1 submission history, not an aggregator's later update date.
summary: Separates individual and organizational cognitive capital from joint human-AI performance. Synthesizes substitution of practice, scaffolding, calibration and organizational aggregation into propositions for future tests.
limitations: Non-exhaustive narrative selection, no quantitative pooling or validated theory. Organizational mechanisms are partly inferred from individual studies; short tasks and adjacent non-generative-AI evidence limit transfer. Much underlying evidence is already in this database.

verification.basis: arXiv identity/version and original PDF review approach, Table 2, limitations and cited Lee/Shen/Bastani papers inspected. The review reports final literature search on 19 October, earlier than its submission. No claim that all references were revalidated here.

title: Task Expansion with Generative AI: Experimental Evidence on Middle-Skilled, Early-Career Workers
date_basis: Institutional record and PDF cover specify October; no exact day inferred from a secondary listing.
summary: Randomly assigns AI access among 673 final-year German IT apprentices. Reports improved performance beyond the curriculum without lower immediate comprehension, testing task expansion rather than speed alone.
limitations: Short occupational tasks and immediate multiple-choice comprehension do not establish durable learning or workplace delivery. Treatment retained internet access during instructed unaided comprehension; authors report compliance checks and exclusion sensitivity. Open answers use blinded LLM grading with teacher-validated rubrics; model-version exposure changed during collection. Working paper, not a completed workplace rollout.

verification.basis: Institutional identity and 106-page PDF checked for sample, within-school randomization, collection October 2025-January 2026, comprehension instructions and access, grading and sensitivity disclosures. References to Shen/Tamkin and Bastani verified. Full appendix and underlying data not audited.

title: Letting AI Formulate the Research Question: Autonomous Research Agents
date_basis: arXiv v1 history and main-text date, not the later digest date.
summary: Reports five consecutive research runs after development, with agent-selected questions, re-computation and AI review. Exposes agenda-setting and reporting choices rather than showing only selected successful papers.
limitations: Five runs, one research model, no ablation and no independent human quality evaluation. Pilot inclusion and choice of review format were amended after results were seen. Re-running the same code is not independent validation; hosted model computation is not local laptop computation. Human instructions and development choices shape the agenda.

verification.basis: arXiv identity and HTML system, evaluation, limitations, AI-involvement statement and selected references inspected. Released code, five generated papers and recordings not independently reproduced. Workshop-level ratings are AI judgments, not actual acceptances.

title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
date_basis: arXiv first submission, 20:25:59 UTC; novelty to this collection does not imply November publication.
summary: Evaluates nine agents on 15 expert-specified follow-up problems. Reports that none of 135 submissions meets all criteria; integrity judgments are a major bottleneck.
limitations: A challenging selected benchmark, not every form of scientific assistance. Scientist-designed rubrics are operationalized through automated judges, not independent human review of all papers. Model, harness and budget affect results. Subsequent reanalysis of these same submissions is not new replication, and judge failure does not establish deliberate fabrication.

verification.basis: 28-author list and submission history verified. Public HTML introduction and protocol inspected alongside original repository's task/trajectory description; HTML rendering is incomplete and full paper/results appendix not claimed read. No benchmark rerun or individual integrity adjudication conducted.

title: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
date_basis: arXiv v1 date and primary HTML header.
summary: Reanalyzes released research-agent judgments and labels numerical claims, distinguishing absent evidence from real values assigned to the wrong experiment. Tests provenance checking and sensitivity to judge choice.
limitations: One reused benchmark, small labeled samples and two in-team annotators, not an independent external panel. A provenance check does not establish scientific correctness, and failure to certify is not falsehood. Judge disagreements were not fully human-adjudicated; relative agent differences may reflect harnesses. A journal name in the manuscript does not establish acceptance.

verification.basis: Author/date, source benchmark, 256-claim labeling scope, held-out evaluation and failure-to-verify distinction inspected. Explicit InnovationEval reference and benchmark snapshot noted. Code and labels not independently rerun; AI assistance in code, drafting and label-consistency review is disclosed.

title: The more you automate, the less you see: Hidden pitfalls of autonomous AI scientists
date_basis: PubMed article date is 5 October; issue date is 13 October. Related preprint first appeared in September 2025.

summary: Studies benchmark selection, leakage, metric misuse and post-hoc selection in two open-source scientific-agent systems. Argues that workflow logs and code expose failures that final manuscripts can conceal.
limitations: Published abstract inspected, not the complete final journal methods. Two systems and controlled pitfalls do not estimate population-wide failure rates or current model ability. Preprint and journal versions are one study family. Kasirzadeh's Google DeepMind employment is disclosed in the journal record.

verification.basis: PubMed authors, DOI/PMID, online/issue dates, abstract and competing interests checked; earlier arXiv/OpenReview identity crosschecked. PNAS endpoint returned 403. No claim to full final-paper inspection or an independent version comparison.

date_basis: Publisher citation_online_date and EPFL institutional issued date agree; repository deposit date is later.

limitations: Public abstract and publisher metadata inspected, not the complete primer. A PDF request returned publisher HTML and is not recorded as a read PDF. Review references overlap existing agent studies; prospective laboratory integration is not measured scientific benefit.

verification.basis: 19 authors, title, DOI and date checked in publisher HTML; EPFL record crosschecked. Public abstract and citation_reference links to AI Scientist and Co-Scientist verified. Full-text methods, figures and supplement not appraised.

Task-level time-saving figures can reflect respondents' total weekly savings rather than task-specific increments.
